title: Panel feedback, heuristics, and backlog grooming — Nov 2025
content:
Context and goal:
- Ran a 90-minute advisory panel (6 external customers + 4 internal observers) to stress-test the proposed Console route config UX (routing policies, fallback model selection, and per-route observability). Objective: surface mental-model mismatches and immediate UI friction that would block adoption by platform teams.

Method and participants:
- Hybrid moderated session; used clickable Figma prototype + short task scenarios (setup a canary route, add fallback, simulate regional outage).
- Customer mix: 2 infra/platform engineers (SaaS), 2 ML infra leads (enterprise), 2 solution architects (regulated finance).
- Observers: product PM (Maya), UX researcher (Jordan), eng lead (Priya), SRE (Ethan).

Quick takeaways (overall):
- Strong interest in explicit "policy precedence" view. Customers repeatedly asked: which policy wins when multiple rules overlap? The prototype buried precedence logic behind nested menus — participants wanted a single, scannable timeline/list.
- Mental model split: "routing = traffic rules" (platforms) vs "routing = model selection + fallback" (ML teams). Need language that bridges both.
- Observability expectations misaligned: users expected token-level cost tradeoffs surfaced immediately when toggling quantized variants. Current mockup shows cost only after saving.
- Error handling UX brittle: when a canary failed in the prototype, error message was generic and left users unsure whether to rollback or reroute.

Detailed observations (verbatim-ish notes):
- Task 1: Create canary route
  * P1 (platform): "Where do I set my percent? I expected a slider next to the route name."
  * P4 (ML lead): paused at "variant" microcopy — thought it meant a training checkpoint not a serving variant.
  * Friction: too many nested modals to link secrets/KMS; they wanted a single setup flow.

- Task 2: Configure fallback
  * Several users attempted to drag variants into a priority list; proto used radio buttons. Drag+drop felt more natural to them.
  * Confusion about "compatible variant" label — users wanted an explicit compatibility matrix (model size, quantization, latency).

- Task 3: Simulate regional outage and observe routing changes
  * Expectation: live timeline + live traffic split visualization. Prototype had a static summary only.
  * Suggestion: show historical fallback events and quick rollback button next to each event.

Heuristic highlights (quick pass, scored 1–5 where 5 = bad):
- Visibility of system status: 3 — no live traffic timeline, only post-fact summary.
- Match between system and real world: 4 — language around variants confused ML roles.
- User control and freedom: 2 — rollback is possible but buried.
- Error prevention: 3 — validation exists but not contextual.
- Recognition rather than recall: 4 — users had to remember variant compatibilities across screens.

Wireframe-specific reactions:
- Routing policy editor: demanded a compact "rules canvas" (mini visual) that surfaces precedence; many sketched a 3-column layout: conditions | priority | action.
- Variant details flyout: wanted a "cost + expected p99 latency" pill at top; suggested green/yellow/red health indicator from last 1h.
- Secrets/KMS flow: several asked for a CLI snippet to paste into infra repos (i.e., give both UI and infra-friendly outputs).

Backlog grooming (prioritized, rough sizing):
- B1: Add policy precedence visual & compact rules canvas — MUST HAVE for platform teams. Size: 8 (sprint points). Owner: UX + FE.
- B2: Replace radio list with drag+drop priority editor for fallbacks — HIGH. Size: 5. Owner: UX.
- B3: Add live traffic timeline + rollback quick action (1-click) — MUST. Size: 13. Owner: Eng + SRE.
- B4: Surface cost/latency estimates inline on variant selector — HIGH. Size: 5. Owner: Product + ML infra.
- B5: Add explicit compatibility matrix modal (model arch, quantization, expected latency bounds) — MED. Size: 3. Owner: Applied ML.
- B6: CLI output for secrets/KMS setup + copyable snippet in UI — LOW. Size: 2. Owner: DevEx.
- B7: Improve error copy for canary failures with suggested actions (rollback, increase capacity, switch variant) — HIGH. Size: 2. Owner: Docs + UX.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Need to validate drag+drop interaction pattern with broader panel (not just 6 customers) — allocate 2 remote tests.
- How aggressive is the team on showing cost estimates? Legal asked to avoid per-token cost leaks vs customers on initial screen. Need policy check.
- Timeline: If we take B1+B3+B4 into next quarter, we should freeze wireframes by Dec 5 to allow Eng ramp in Jan.

Next steps (action items):
- Maya: refine wireframe for policy canvas (due Nov 26).
- Jordan: run quick usability follow-up focused on drag+drop (2 remote sessions, target Dec 3).
- Priya: spike on live timeline feasibility (estimate infra effort and storage impact) — report Nov 28.
- Ethan: draft improved canary failure messages and create JIRA for rollout.
- Samira: check compliance/legal on cost surfaced in UI and record answer in PRD.

Appendix (raw quotes and microcopy ideas):
- Microcopy: "Fallback priority (1 = primary, 3 = lowest). Drag to reorder."
- Quote: "We don't want surprises at midnight — show me two things: what changed and how to undo it." — Platform lead
- Quick sketch idea: three-column rule canvas with keyboard shortcuts: N = new condition, D = duplicate rule, R = reorder.

Status: draft notes from the panel; prepping a condensed one-pager for exec sync.
